questions.question: Which Boolean operator should be used to include users who meet all of the following criteria: opened email in last 30 days AND made purchase in last 60 days?
questions.explanation: The AND operator returns users who satisfy every condition, matching the requirement for users meeting both criteria simultaneously.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a standard filter and a custom attribute filter in Braze segmentation?
options: Standard filters are only for event properties
Custom attributes are defined by marketers and can be any data type
Standard filters cannot be combined with Boolean logic
Custom attributes are automatically updated by Braze
questions.explanation: Custom attributes are user-defined fields that marketers populate with any data type, unlike predefined standard filters provided by Braze.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between A/B testing and multivariate testing?
options: A/B testing is faster but less accurate
A/B testing examines one variable; multivariate testing examines two or more variables simultaneously
Multivariate testing is only for email
A/B testing requires a larger sample size
questions.explanation: A/B testing compares single variations (one variable changed), while multivariate testing tests multiple variables at once to find optimal combinations.

questions.question: Approximately how many users per variant should you target for 95% confidence in your test results?
questions.explanation: As a general guide, you need around 15,000 users per variant (including control) to achieve 95% confidence in test results, though this can vary by use case.

questions.question: True or False: You can modify a campaign's parameters after a multivariate test has begun.
questions.explanation: False. Changing parameters after the test starts compromises the experiment, and Braze immediately disables it to preserve data integrity.

questions.question: What is 'Winning Variant' optimization in Braze A/B testing?
options: Sending the best-performing variant from the initial test to remaining users
Randomly selecting variants for all users
Testing only the most popular variant
questions.explanation: Winning Variant optimization sends the top-performing variant from the initial test to the remaining audience members who didn't receive the test.

questions.question: What does 'Personalized Variant' optimization do differently from 'Winning Variant'?
options: It sends the variant users are most likely to engage with, based on their characteristics
questions.explanation: Personalized Variant analyzes which variant each user is most likely to engage with based on their individual characteristics and custom events.

questions.question: What is a random bucket number in Braze?
options: A user attribute for creating uniformly distributed random segments
questions.explanation: Random bucket numbers are user attributes used to create uniformly distributed random segments for fair audience allocation in tests and campaigns.

questions.question: What does 'frequency capping' accomplish in Braze messaging?
options: Limits how often users receive messages to prevent message fatigue
questions.explanation: Frequency capping controls how many messages a user receives within a specific timeframe, preventing audience fatigue and improving engagement.

questions.question: True or False: Channel subscription states should be leveraged when determining which channel to send to users.
questions.explanation: True. Respecting channel subscription states ensures you only send messages through channels users have opted into, improving compliance and engagement.

questions.question: What are Experiment Paths in Braze Canvas used for?
options: Testing multiple Canvas paths against each other with control groups to measure performance
questions.explanation: Experiment Paths let you test different journey variations within a Canvas against a control group to identify the highest-performing paths.

questions.question: What risk does using randomized paths in Experiment Paths pose to test validity?
options: Control group contamination when users re-enter and are reassigned
questions.explanation: Randomized path assignments on re-entry can contaminate the control group with treatment users, invalidating experiment results since users aren't assigned consistently.

questions.question: What is 'segment re-eligibility' in Braze?
options: Determining how soon a user can re-enter a campaign after receiving a message
questions.explanation: Re-eligibility rules control whether and when users who previously received a campaign can qualify for it again based on rule changes.

questions.question: What is 'statistical confidence' in the context of Braze testing?
options: How sure Braze is that a variant is genuinely different from control, increasing over time
The percentage of users who engage
The cost of running the test
questions.explanation: Confidence measures how sure the platform is that observed differences between variants are real and not due to random chance, increasing as test runs longer.

questions.question: Which of the following are variables you can test in a multivariate test? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Multivariate tests can vary multiple elements like subject lines, images, CTA button colors, send times, and content combinations to find optimal configurations.

questions.question: What does BrazeAI Variant Selection do in push campaigns?
options: Automatically runs experiments and optimizes for best engagement results
questions.explanation: BrazeAI Variant Selection automatically optimizes single send or recurring push A/B tests by experimenting and selecting the best-performing variant.

questions.question: True or False: You can combine multiple Boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) in a single segment.
questions.explanation: True. Complex segments require combining multiple Boolean operators to create precise audience definitions based on multiple conditions.

questions.question: What does low confidence in test results typically indicate?
options: Sample size is too small and should be enlarged for future tests
questions.explanation: Low confidence signals insufficient sample size. Larger test groups increase confidence and the ability to detect meaningful differences between variants.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using Canvas for campaign management over standalone campaigns?
options: Multi-step journeys with branching logic based on user behavior and lifecycle stage
questions.explanation: Canvas enables sophisticated multi-step journeys where users follow different paths based on their behavior, characteristics, and engagement—impossible in single campaigns.

questions.question: What is Liquid personalization in Braze?
options: A templating language for dynamic message personalization using user data
questions.explanation: Liquid is a templating language that allows dynamic personalization—inserting user attributes, custom properties, and data into messages in real-time.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing sample size for multivariate testing?
options: Number of variants (more variants require larger groups) and desired confidence level
questions.explanation: Sample size depends on number of variants (more variants = fewer users per variant = larger total group needed) and target confidence percentage.

questions.question: True or False: If you find no clear difference between variant performance, the test strategy needs adjustment.
questions.explanation: True. No significant difference often indicates the variant differences were too subtle, the sample was too small, or the test strategy should be reconsidered.

questions.question: What does 'segment extension' do in Braze?
options: Refines audience segments using advanced filters and conditions
questions.explanation: Segment extensions allow you to refine your target audiences using additional filters and behavioral conditions beyond basic segmentation.

questions.question: What outcome metrics should be tracked when evaluating Canvas performance?
options: Conversion rates, retention, engagement by channel, and retention metrics
questions.explanation: Canvas effectiveness should be measured by real business outcomes: conversion rates, customer retention, channel engagement, and lifetime value impact.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'conversion-based suppression' in messaging?
options: Automatically stopping campaigns once users complete the target action to prevent irrelevant followups
questions.explanation: Conversion-based suppression stops messaging to users who've already completed the campaign goal, improving experience and preventing wasted sends.

questions.question: When setting up a multivariate test, what must be held constant to maintain valid results?
options: External marketing factors (special sales, seasonal events) that could influence variant perception
questions.explanation: Holding constant means no other marketing factors should change during the test. A sale ending mid-test or seasonal events can invalidate results.

questions.question: True or False: Custom attributes must be updated manually by marketers for each user.
questions.explanation: True. Custom attributes are marketer-defined and must be populated by the marketer or system through SDK/API, unlike auto-tracked standard attributes.

questions.question: What key insight can multivariate test results provide for future campaigns?
options: Only the best subject line works
How different message elements resonate with audiences and what combinations drive best results
questions.explanation: Multivariate results reveal which message combinations resonate most with audiences, enabling data-driven decisions on messaging strategy and personalization.

questions.question: How does multichannel orchestration in Canvas improve customer experience?
options: Coordinating push, email, SMS, and in-app within a single workflow for consistent, timely experiences
questions.explanation: Canvas orchestration coordinates messages across channels in a unified journey, ensuring consistent brand experience and optimal timing for each touchpoint.

questions.question: What is a practical consideration when deciding between A/B and multivariate testing?
options: A/B tests work with smaller traffic; multivariate needs more users and becomes harder to manage with many variant combinations
questions.explanation: A/B tests are simpler and work with smaller audiences; multivariate tests need larger groups and become complex with many variable combinations.
